Derive handler arguments with `InferToolParams`; keep the schema as the single source of truth for validation and types. 3. Define the response contract and output schema for read tools in `utils/response-contracts.ts`. 4. Register the definition through `tools/register.ts`, use the existing `ToolRuntime` error/observation path, and add a co-located test. 5. Measure token cost when tool descriptions or schemas materially change: `pnpm run measure:tokens`. Handlers receive inferred arguments. Keep manual argument casts, `any`, and `unknown` out of tool-handler code. Reuse the existing error policy, `withErrorHandling` path, response contracts, and safe diagnostics rather than creating parallel response or error formats. ## Secrets and runtime behavior Use `HEVY_API_KEY` through `.env` or the process environment. Keep `.env` and real keys untracked, and keep keys out of command-line arguments, URLs, logs, fixtures, screenshots, and error messages. Deterministic unit, mocked MCP, contract, stdio, package, and performance lanes use fake credentials and do not need a live key. Live Hevy lanes require a valid `HEVY_API_KEY`. The Node executable defaults to stdio and also supports local Streamable HTTP with `--transport http`; inspect `packages/node/README.md` or `--help` before changing transport behavior. The Worker serves stateless Streamable HTTP at `POST /mcp`, authenticates the request bearer value, and keeps OAuth optional behind the `OAUTH_KV` binding. Read the Worker section of `CONTRIBUTING.md` before changing deployment, origin, authentication, or OAuth behavior. ## Changesets and release identity Before every commit, classify the diff and run: ```bash pnpm run check:changeset ``` A change under `packages/*`, a runtime-visible behavior change, a workspace dependency change, or `cloudflare.config.ts` requires a non-empty bump Changeset. Name the changed package and every transitive shipped consumer from `repository/topology.json`; do not couple unrelated packages. The current cascade is: - `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client` -> `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client`, `@hevy-mcp/operations`, `@hevy-mcp/core`, `hevy-mcp`, `@hevy-mcp/worker`, `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli`. - `@hevy-mcp/operations` -> `@hevy-mcp/operations`, `@hevy-mcp/core`, `hevy-mcp`, `@hevy-mcp/worker`, `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli`. - `@hevy-mcp/core` -> `@hevy-mcp/core`, `hevy-mcp`, `@hevy-mcp/worker`, `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli`. - Node-only, Worker-only, and CLI-only changes bump only their respective package; `cloudflare.config.ts` is a Worker change. Core, client, operations, and Worker are private but versioned for internal release/deployment identity. Node and CLI are public. Merge the automated `changeset-release/main` Version Packages pull request on the routine cadence (weekly by default); reserve off-cycle releases for security fixes and high-impact user-facing bugs. An entirely no-release, repository-only change may use an eligible empty Changeset via `npx changeset --empty`; docs, CI, repository-only tests/tooling, and chores qualify only when no release trigger is present. An empty Changeset never accompanies a release trigger. Stage the Changeset before committing. ## Validation workflow For source changes, run the narrow relevant lane and the unit suite. Before a pull request, use the repository baseline from `CONTRIBUTING.md`: ```bash mise exec -- pnpm run check mise exec -- pnpm run check:types mise exec -- pnpm run build mise exec -- pnpm run test:pr mise exec -- pnpm run test:performance mise exec -- pnpm run check:changeset ``` Useful focused checks include: - `pnpm run test:stdio` after MCP SDK, stdio, lifecycle, or Node transport changes. `packages/node/src/utils/stdio-observability.ts` uses private MCP SDK fields, so inspect compatibility after every SDK upgrade. - `pnpm run test:worker`, `pnpm run test:worker-http`, and `pnpm run worker:dry-run` after Worker changes. - `pnpm run test:pack` or `pnpm run test:pack:cli` after package entry point, binary, manifest, or published-file changes. - `pnpm run check:server-manifest` after server metadata changes. - `pnpm run check:boundaries` after workspace dependency or runtime-boundary changes. `pnpm run test:unit` is the deterministic default for local source work. `npm test` builds first and runs broad Vitest discovery; it is not a substitute for the named PR lanes. Integration, live, nightly, and live Worker commands are credential-gated and should be run only when the relevant safe credentials and environment are available. Known environment-dependent operations: - `pnpm run openapi` needs network access to the upstream Hevy API and may fail with `ENOTFOUND api.hevyapp.com` in a sandbox. - `pnpm run inspect` may time out without a correctly configured MCP client or browser environment. Treat all other documented checks, including `pnpm run check:types`, as real failures to investigate. ## Completion checklist Before reporting completion, confirm that the diff is focused, tests and checks for the changed paths passed (or their limitations are explicit), generated output is synchronized, the release requirement is satisfied, and `git status --short --branch` shows only intended files on the feature branch. This repo has the entire-graph code graph installed. Before exploring code with grep/find/whole-file reads, read .entire/graph-agent.md — resolution-first guidance for using graph retrieval, focused source inspection, and verification. @.entire/graph-agent.md # Ultracite Code Standards This project uses **Ultracite**, a zero-config preset that enforces strict code quality standards through automated formatting and linting. ## Quick Reference - **Format code**: `pnpm run fix` - **Check for issues**: `pnpm run check` - **Diagnose setup**: `pnpm exec ultracite doctor` Oxlint + Oxfmt (the underlying engine) provides robust linting and formatting. Most issues are automatically fixable. --- ## Core Principles Write code that is **accessible, performant, type-safe, and maintainable**. Focus on clarity and explicit intent over brevity. ### Type Safety & Explicitness - Use explicit types for function parameters and return values when they enhance clarity - Prefer `unknown` over `any` when the type is genuinely unknown - Use const assertions (`as const`) for immutable values and literal types - Leverage TypeScript's type narrowing instead of type assertions - Use meaningful variable names instead of magic numbers - extract constants with descriptive names ### Modern JavaScript/TypeScript - Use arrow functions for callbacks and short functions - Prefer `for...of` loops over `.forEach()` and indexed `for` loops - Use optional chaining (`?.`) and nullish coalescing (`??`) for safer property access - Prefer template literals over string concatenation - Use destructuring for object and array assignments - Use `const` by default, `let` only when reassignment is needed, never `var` ### Async & Promises - Always `await` promises in async functions - don't forget to use the return value - Use `async/await` syntax instead of promise chains for better readability - Handle errors appropriately in async code with try-catch blocks - Don't use async functions as Promise executors ### React & JSX - Use function components over class components - Call hooks at the top level only, never conditionally - Specify all dependencies in hook dependency arrays correctly - Use the `key` prop for elements in iterables (prefer unique IDs over array indices) - Nest children between opening and closing tags instead of passing as props - Don't define components inside other components - Use semantic HTML and ARIA attributes for accessibility: - Provide meaningful alt text for images - Use proper heading hierarchy - Add labels for form inputs - Include keyboard event handlers alongside mouse events - Use semantic elements (`

## Concrete candidate refactor points for deeper Effect adoption

1. **Lifecycle as a scoped Effect program** — `runNodeLifecycle` (`src/utils/node-lifecycle.ts:169-227`) is a manual scope: install exception tracking → run `start` → install shutdown → on exit, cleanup + `flushTelemetry`. This maps directly to `Effect.scoped` + `Effect.acquireRelease` (exception-tracking install/remove at `telemetry.ts:47-90`; shutdown install/cleanup at `graceful-shutdown.ts:71-198`), with the failure taxonomy (`LIFECYCLE_FAILURE_TAXONOMY`, lines 25-51) becoming a typed `Data.TaggedError` hierarchy instead of string phases.

2. **Graceful shutdown → `Scope` + interruption** — `graceful-shutdown.ts` re-implements signal handling, forced-exit deadline (`FORCED_EXIT_TIMEOUT_MS = 5_000`, line 45), and idempotent completion. `Effect.acquireRelease` for listener install, `Effect.timeout`/`race` for the forced exit, and fiber interruption for `cancel.abort(...)` (line 119) would remove the `shutdownSettled`/`completionReported` flags and the `closePromise` memoization pattern duplicated in `streamable-http.ts:757-795`.

3. **HTTP server session graph → `Scope`-per-session + `Effect` server loop** — `streamable-http.ts` manages `sessions`/`pendingSessions`/`initializationControllers`/`cleanupErrors` by hand. Each `HttpSession` (lines 123-132) is an acquired resource (transport + MCP server + `AbortController` + idle timer) with release in `closeSession` (lines 464-503). Candidates:
   - `Effect.acquireRelease` per session; `Scope` per session and per server; `Effect.allSettled`-equivalents (`Effect.all` with `ConcurrencyOptions`/ `Effect.forEachPar` + `Exit`) replace `Promise.allSettled` + manual `aggregateErrors` (lines 400-403).
   - `readBody` (lines 259-337) is a stream decode with size limit, timeout, and abort — maps to a `Stream`/`Sink` or `Effect.async` with proper interruption instead of the listener state machine.
   - Idle eviction timer (lines 444-462) → `Schedule`/`Effect.timeout` on a per-session fiber.
   - Admission control (`reserveInitialization`, lines 573-626) → `Semaphore` (`Effect.makeSemaphore`) for `maxInitializing`/`maxSessions` instead of Set-size checks.

4. **Telemetry init/flush → Layer** — `telemetry.ts` runs provider construction at import time (lines 164-240) and exports ambient `tracer`/`meter` (lines 265-266). This is a natural `Layer.effect(TelemetryService, ...)` with `Scope`-finalized `forceFlush`/shutdown, replacing `flushTelemetry`'s manual `Promise.race` timeout (lines 242-262) with `Effect.timeout`. It would also remove the import-order constraint documented in `runtime.ts:1-3`.

5. **Ad-hoc logging → `Effect.log*` / Logger** — `console.error`/`console.log` appear at `cli.ts:8,10`, `runtime.ts:186,227,259,263,275,329,333,363`, `streamable-http.ts:464,757` area (request/cleanup failure logs), `stdio-observability.ts:284` (`reportStdinParseFailure`), `debug.ts:139` (`process.stderr.write`). These are all candidate `Effect.logError`/`logInfo` with a custom stderr `Logger`, letting log level/redaction ride on Effect's logging instead of per-call try/catch.

6. **Metrics → `Metric` module** — `metrics.ts` module-level OTel counters plus call sites like `serverStartups.add(1, ...)` (`node-lifecycle.ts:190`), `httpAdmissionRejections.add` (`streamable-http.ts:405-413` with defensive try/catch), `sessionStarted/sessionEnded` (`mcp-session-observability.ts:214,272`) could be `Metric.counter(...)`/`Effect.withMetric` once a telemetry Layer exists. The defensive "telemetry must never affect behavior" try/catch blocks scattered across `tool-observer.ts` (`bestEffort`, lines 208-214), `hevy-client-observability.ts`, `failure-reporter.ts` would collapse into Effect's typed error channel + sandboxing.

7. **Retry/timeout → `Schedule`** — `version-check.ts` fetch uses `AbortSignal.timeout(REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS)` (line 161); `runtime.ts` startup probe uses `maxGetRetries: 0` + manual deadline (`STARTUP_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS`, lines 89, 166-173). If node ever owns retry/timeout policy, `Schedule` + `Effect.timeout` apply; today most retry lives in `hevy-client` (already Effect internally).

8. **Startup API-key probe** — `validateApiKey` (`runtime.ts:158-193`) is a Promise probe with bespoke error parsing (`validationErrorSchema`, `getHttpStatus`, `getSafeValidationDiagnostic`). As an Effect it could compose with the client's existing `RequestEffect` error types instead of re-deriving status/code from `unknown`.

9. **`AsyncLocalStorage` + module-global session → `FiberRef`/`Context`** — `mcp-session-observability.ts` uses ALS (line 51) plus a mutable `activeStdioSession` global (line 73) with explicit cleanup (lines 268-271); `sdk-observability.ts` uses two more ALS instances (lines 62-65). `FiberRef.currentContext`-style propagation would make context flow through fibers instead of Node's async-hooks with a process-global fallback.

10. **Signal/env/config parsing** — `config.ts` (`parseConfig`/`assertApiKey` throwing `MissingHevyApiKeyError`), `arguments.ts` throwing parsers, and scattered `process.env` reads (`telemetry.ts:123-137`, `streamable-http.ts:76,441`, `hevy-client-observability.ts:115`, `failure-reporter.ts:90-92`, `version-check.ts:65`) → `Config` module with typed `Config.Error` instead of thrown `Error`s.

11. **Test hooking** — `version-check.ts` already ships a hand-rolled DI bag (`VersionCheckDependencies`/`SchedulerDependencies`, lines 36-70) purely for testability; `Layer` would replace it.

## Promise boundary: how node consumes core today

- `createHevyMcpServer` (`packages/core/src/server.ts:58-102`) is **synchronous** and internally does `Effect.runSync(Cache.make(...))` at `server.ts:74-80` and builds a layer context via `Effect.runSync(Scope.make())` + `Effect.runSync(Scope.provide(scope)(Layer.build(layer)))` at `tool-runtime.ts:94-95`. The scope is intentionally leaked ("outlives this call") with no finalizer — node never closes it; server close only calls SDK `close()`. A `Scope`-owned runtime handed to the adapter (closed during graceful shutdown) is an obvious fix.
- Each tool invocation crosses back via `Effect.runPromise(provided)` at `tool-runtime.ts:200` (`runToolEffect`), wrapped by `withErrorHandling`.
- Node's `ToolObserver.run` contract is `(operation: () => Promise<T>) => Promise<T>` (`tool-observer.ts:224-240`), and `hevy-client`'s `onRequestStart` returns `{ run: (op: () => Promise<T>) => Promise<T>, finish }` (`hevy-client-observability.ts:120-131`; interface at `packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client-kubb.ts:160`). Both are Promise-shaped seams where node wraps spans around operations — if the core/client boundaries ever expose `Effect`-typed hooks, these two adapter files become thin OTel `Layer`s instead of closure-based span managers.

## Public export surface that hides Effect types

`packages/node/package.json` exports only `"."` → `dist/index.mjs` (`src/index.ts`), exposing:
- `createNodeMcpServer({ apiKey }, transport?, lifecycleSignal?): Promise<McpServer>` (`index.ts:22-40`)
- `runStdioServer(): Promise<void>` and `runServer(): Promise<void>` (`index.ts:46-57`)

All three are pure Promise signatures with no Effect types; the SDK `McpServer` return type keeps core's `Layer`/`Scope`/`Cache` internals invisible. `bin` points at `dist/cli.mjs` (`src/cli.ts`). The embedding contract (`index.ts` header comment, lines 12-19) explicitly forbids startup side effects in this module, so any Effect adoption must keep the entry side-effect-free (e.g. return a lazy program or keep the Promise façade over `Effect.runPromise`).

## Notable constraints for any refactor

- `stdio-observability.ts` and `sdk-observability.ts` deliberately patch **private MCP SDK fields** (`_ondata`, `_readBuffer`, `_requestHandlers`, `createToolError`); AGENTS.md requires compatibility review after every SDK upgrade — Effect refactors must not disturb those patch points.
- `telemetry.ts` must remain importable before everything else until init moves behind a Layer; `runtime.ts:1-3` documents this ordering requirement.
- `index.ts` must stay side-effect-free (embedding contract + its test enforces it).
- The `hevy-mcp` package bundles `@hevy-mcp/core`, `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client`, `@hevy-mcp/operations` into `dist` (`tsdown.config.ts` `alwaysBundle`), so adding an `effect` runtime dependency to node means either declaring it as a runtime dep or bundling it — a package-boundary decision (`pnpm run check:boundaries`).
